subject: Attribution carve-outs & embargo window — MSA / Order Form coordination
messages:
From: Sam Rogers <sam.rogers@brightsky.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: BrightSky Legal <legal@brightsky.com>, BrightSky Marketing <marketing@brightsky.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Attribution carve-outs & embargo window — MSA / Order Form coordination

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal asked us to confirm a couple of items before we can sign the MSA + order form:

1) Embargo window: we need to make sure that any public announcement referencing BrightSky (press release, blog post, social) is subject to a 30-day embargo from go-live unless we explicitly agree to a shorter window in writing. Is that acceptable?

2) Attribution vs. case study: marketing would like permissive quote usage (short testimonial quote + logo) for joint materials, but legal prefers more restrictive language that requires BrightSky approval for any case study or slide-deck level attribution. Can we propose a middle ground in the MSA: logo + one-line customer quote OK without additional approval, but any extended case study or customer story requires pre-approval?

3) Logo usage: we have a couple of co-branding treatments that need to be cleared (see attached press-asset-specs.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood’s recommended usage rules (size, placement, color) so we can map them into the order form?

Attached: BrightSky_MSA_Redline_v2.docx (redlines from our side). Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute sync if helpful.

Best,
Sam Rogers
Head of Strategic Partnerships
BrightSky

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Rogers <sam.rogers@brightsky.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>, BrightSky Legal <legal@brightsky.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Attribution carve-outs & embargo window — MSA / Order Form coordination

Sam —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Quick responses inline:

- Embargo window: 30 days is a bit conservative for our typical launches; we usually ask for a 7–14 day notification window so we can coordinate quotes and finalize screenshots. For enterprise customers with joint announcements we can accept a 30-day embargo as an option in the order form but want a carve-out that allows Redwood to publish a short launch note (1–2 sentences) after 14 days if there has been no feedback.

- Attribution vs. case study: your proposal sounds reasonable. Suggested clause language (high level):
  • Permitted: logo use (per spec) and up to one short customer quote (<= 30 words) for marketing materials without additional approval.
  • Controlled: any case study, benchmark, or extended customer story requires written pre-approval from the customer.

- Logo usage: we’ll map our default brand spec into the order form. See attached BrightSky_MSA_Redline_v3.docx — I’ve incorporated a brand-spec reference and a short approval flow (Marketing approves minor uses; legal signs off on case studies).

Next steps: I’ve uploaded a suggested redline and a short mutual action plan (attached). Marissa — can you review the proposed 14-day fallback wording? Dev — can you confirm there are no product screenshots in the standard onboarding pack that would require earlier approval?

If this is acceptable to BrightSky legal, we can move to a quick DocuSign for the MSA and order form edits and keep the detailed logo spec as an appendix.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: BrightSky_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (redline with brand-spec appendix)
Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Attribution carve-outs & embargo window — MSA / Order Form coordination

Irene / Dev — quick notes from marketing:

• 14-day fallback is fine but request we add a line that allows BrightSky Marketing to request a 7-day review turnaround for marketing collateral where timing is critical (e.g., trade shows). We would commit to that SLA on our side.
• On the quote: we prefer a mechanism where the customer can pre-approve a \"bank\" of short quotes during onboarding to avoid last-minute holds. If legal insists, we can capture 2–3 templated quotes during onboarding and store them in the account folder.
• Screenshots: Dev — can you confirm whether the onboarding pack includes any sample UIs? If so, we need an explicit clause that any screenshots that contain PII or customer-specific configuration will require approval.

Irene — happy to take point on the approval flow language in the order form appendix. I’ll add the templated-quote section to BrightSky_MSA_Redline_v3.docx and push a new version by EOD.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Growth Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Attribution carve-outs & embargo window — MSA / Order Form coordination

Sam — quick technical confirmation:

• Standard onboarding pack includes 2 UI screenshots (generic examples). We do not include BrightSky live data or PII.
• If BrightSky wants screenshots of their configured instance, that would require approval; we can flag any request as \"customer-specific asset\" in the appendix so it routes to legal for sign-off.

Sam — thanks for the redline. If BrightSky legal signs off on the 14-day fallback + templated-quote approach, we can accept the 30-day embargo as an optional setting in the order form (customer chooses 14-day vs 30-day) and move the MSA redline to DocuSign.

Karthik — can you run the final clause language by legal counsel and, if OK, I’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope tomorrow.

Best,
Dev Patel
Sr. Product Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference
